QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_49

question.text: SEBI has mandated the exercise of 'stewardship responsibilities' by all AIFs with respect to their investments in LISTED companies. This includes:

answer.text: Outsourcing all voting to a third-party proxy advisory firm without oversight
Buying and selling shares rapidly to maximise short-term alpha
Monitoring and actively engaging with investee companies on performance, strategy, corporate governance, ESG risks/opportunities, capital structure — via discussions, board interactions, and voting
Avoiding any contact with investee-company management

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI Stewardship Circular CIR/CFD/CMD1/168/2019 (Dec 24, 2019) and March 2020 update, AIFs must shoulder stewardship for LISTED investments — monitor and engage on performance, strategy, governance, remuneration, ESG, capital structure via management discussions, board meeting interactions, and voting. The Trap: Rapid trading and no-contact approaches violate the stewardship spirit. Pure outsourcing of voting — even to a proxy adviser — is discouraged without oversight. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests stewardship. Stewardship is tested across XIX-A, XIX-B, XIX-C, XIX-D, XXI-B. Manager's Pro-Tip: Publish your stewardship policy on the AIF's website and include an annual stewardship report in the investor quarterly pack. Track and disclose voting: % resolutions voted, % voted with management, % abstained.
